source_text:
We have now shown that for any $
u$ with $
u^q 
eq 
u$ the representation $Y_
u$ with the same character as

$$W_1 \otimes V_{\alpha,1} - V_{\alpha,1} - \operatorname{Ind}_K^G \mathbb{C}_
u$$

exists and is irreducible. These characters are distinct for distinct pairs $(\alpha, 
u)$ (up to switching $
u 	o 
u^q$), so there are $ rac{q(q-1)}{2}$ such representations, each of dimension $q - 1$. These representations are called complementary series representations.

We have thus found $q - 1$ 1-dimensional representations of $G$, $ rac{q(q-1)}{2}$ principal series representations, and $ rac{q(q-1)}{2}$ complementary series representations, for a total of $q^2 - 1$ representations, i.e., the number of conjugacy classes in $G$. This implies that we have in fact found all irreducible representations of $GL_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$.
